speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with a loss of consciousness; to begin my assessment, how long were you unconscious and did you have any witnesses to the event?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: That loss of consciousness occurring immediately after urination is a very specific clue. Did you experience any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath right before you passed out? Also, do you have a history of heart disease or high blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Commotio Cordis.

The loss of consciousness occurring immediately after micturating suggests a Valsalva maneuver, but the rapid return of consciousness without confusion or injury makes a cardiac arrhythmia like ventricular fibrillation (commotio cordis) or a neurogenic cause (vasovagal) more likely than traumatic asystole.
